newsitem.title: USA: LDC debts mixed, defying U.S. Treasuries selloff.
newsitem.headline: LDC debts mixed, defying U.S. Treasuries selloff.

text.p: Emerging market debts escaped unscathed from the collateral damage of falling U.S. treasuries to trade mixed late Thursday.
"Spreads have come in five to 10 basis points," said a trader, noting that while par bonds suffered somewhat, Argentina FRB and Brazil both held well.
Argentina FRBs ARFLC05=RR rose 3/8 to bid 86-7/8 and Brazil C BR8D14=RR eased 1/8 to 73-7/8 bid, while the benchmark 30-year U.S. T-bond lost 1-15/32 points to yield 6.51 percent.
Traders said Brazil EI BRFLD06=RR in particular was well bid, because, as a floater, it was less sensitive to Treasury swings. It gained 1/4 to 87 bid.
Omar Borla, chief Latin America economist at Robert Flemings Inc, said Argentina and Brazil appealed to investors because of their respective political outlooks.

President Cardoso's re-election in Brazil appeared to be garnering support and Argentina's stronger-than-expected economic recovery would strengthen President Menem's hands in running the government, he said.
Ecuador Bradies suffered more selling amid growing doubts on President Abdala Bucaram's ability to push through structural reforms, traders said.
Ecuador Pars ECPARS=RR lost 3/4 to 46-1/2 bid and PDI ECPDI=RR shed 5/8 to 68-3/4 bid.

Bulgaria continued the bull run as more players jumped on the bandwagon on hopes that the adoption of a currency board would induce the International Monetary Fund to loosen its purse strings on withheld loans.
"It is a small market," said a trader. "With several traders of $10 (million) to $20 million, the prices could jump a lot."
But a buyside source put the chance of implementing a currency board at 60-40. "The Socialists are divided," he said. "They may not get the support they need."
Bulgaria FLRB BGFLIRB=RR soared 3 points to 40-1/2 bid."
